name: Nelco Ltd
tagline: Rs ~2,100 Cr Tata Power subsidiary and India VSAT market leader -- FY25 profit collapsed (~Rs 4-10 Cr, EBITDA margin ~20% -> ~11%), core revenue declining, no concalls -- the entire bull case is unproven LEO / satellite-broadband optionality against a tiny (~Rs 1,000 Cr) domestic VSAT TAM
business_overview: Nelco (NSE: NELCO), a Tata Power subsidiary and part of the Tata Group since 1940, is India's leading VSAT / satellite-communications service provider, serving banking / ATM, oil & gas, defence, maritime and enterprise-WAN customers, with adjacencies in integrated security & surveillance and satcom projects (via subsidiary Nelco Network Products). It has a 10-year national VSAT VNO licence and partnerships with Telesat, Intelsat, Panasonic and, for LEO, a stated tie-up with Starlink.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 305-312 Cr (FY25); ~6-7% CAGR over a decade; core revenue -12% YoY in Q1
~Rs 4-10 Cr FY25, down ~58% YoY; consolidated PBT -60% YoY
~19% / ~21% (stale -- pre-collapse; now far lower on TTM PAT)
Rs 642 - 1,503; ~16x book, triple-digit P/E on collapsed earnings
fundamentals_narrative: FY25 was a sharp deterioration: consolidated PBT down ~61%, standalone PBT down ~72%, EBITDA margin roughly halved, dividend cut over 50%. Core VSAT revenue is shrinking, and the company holds no quarterly concalls -- execution visibility comes only from annual reports and filings. The bull case rests entirely on LEO / satellite-broadband becoming a large Indian market and Nelco capturing it, but the domestic enterprise VSAT market is only ~Rs 750-1,000 Cr, Nelco is already near-leader within it, and the LEO economics are being set by Starlink / OneWeb with Jio and Airtel as the scaled distribution partners. At ~16x book and a triple-digit P/E on collapsed earnings, the price already embeds a successful pivot.
technical_read: Not pulled -- wide 52-week band (642 to 1,503); no dedicated technical read this pass.
sentiment_summary: Dedicated VP thread (topic 198557), 29 posts Jun-2025 to Mar-2026, no trusted-user participation. Discussion is thoughtful but net-skeptical: recurring questions on how large the Indian satcom TAM can really be, whether Nelco has anything preventing telcos / new satcom entrants from taking the market, and concern about the FY25 profit collapse. Constructive notes on the VNO licence, Nelco Network Products as a new growth driver, and 2020/2022 space-sector reforms, but no high-conviction buy call. Latest activity (Mar-2026) is a factual note on space-sector reform, not a thesis update.
community_signal: No trusted-user coverage. Untrusted X-triage lead (@BeatTheStreet10). VP thread sentiment mixed-to-skeptical on TAM and competitive positioning.
bse_notes: Tata Power subsidiary (ownership via Tata Power, not Tata Sons directly -- some thread speculation about future group restructuring). 10-year VSAT VNO licence granted Jun-2025. FY25 dividend cut >50%. No going-concern / governance red flags.
bull_case: Tata-group parentage, India VSAT market leadership, 10-year national VNO licence
LEO / satellite-broadband optionality -- Starlink partnership, potential rural / enterprise connectivity expansion if the market inflects
Nelco Network Products (hardware / rentals / projects) emerging as a secondary growth driver
bear_case: FY25 earnings collapse -- consolidated PBT -60% YoY, EBITDA margin ~20% -> ~11%, dividend cut >50%; core VSAT revenue declining
Domestic enterprise VSAT TAM is tiny (~Rs 750-1,000 Cr) and Nelco is already near-leader -- limited headroom
LEO economics set by Starlink / OneWeb with Jio / Airtel as scaled distributors -- Nelco risks disintermediation
No quarterly concalls -- poor execution visibility
~16x book and triple-digit P/E on collapsed earnings -- pivot already priced
verdict_headline: Declining VSAT leader with a tiny TAM, collapsed FY25 earnings and no concalls, priced for an unproven LEO pivot -- 'neither', conviction Low
verdict_reasoning: Space sector is on the priority-2 theme list, but this was processed as an external lead, not a discovery theme hit, and the exposure is domestic enterprise VSAT (shrinking) plus speculative LEO distribution, not a differentiated space-tech capability.

four_box score 1.0 -> 'neither' (hard). tailwind weak (LEO / satcom is a real theme but Nelco's core is declining and its LEO role is unproven), tam no (~Rs 2,100 Cr mcap against a ~Rs 1,000 Cr domestic VSAT market where it already leads -- cannot get 10x/100x headroom), moat weak (Tata brand + VNO licence + B2B relationships, but telcos partnering Starlink directly threaten disintermediation), valuation no (~16x book, triple-digit P/E on collapsed earnings). No live-inflection carve-out -- the recent quarters are a negative inflection.

Conviction Low. Not a red flag -- it is a solvent Tata company -- but declining core economics, a structurally small TAM, no concall visibility and a demanding valuation make this a 'neither'. Re-check only if LEO / broadband revenue becomes a reported, material line and core margins recover.
